Greetings, I am No Talent Redmage and I'm playing absolute shit, no seriously, there's nothing here to see but shit. I'm playing Revolution X for the Snes or more accurately trying not to collapse on the floor and cry in the fetal position or hunt down something underneath the sink to make the hurting stop. (I heard Clorox helps though you can use a bottle of Jack for the less suicide inclined)

A bit of history for the morbidly curious, see Acclaim released an arcade game with quite possibly the dumbest story and digitized graphics this side of a particular jaguar fighting game starring a cross fireball shooting sportsman. The game was fun in arcades for a little bit though your quarters were much better used on games like X-men Since it had reliability and was much higher quality.

Essentially, an authoritarian entity called NoN has outlawed all fun. Comics, video games and rock music are all now illegal. In order to protest this Aerosmith has a concert at Club X and then puts signs and pamplets everywhere that they are there performing. (Self martyring is easy I guess). You decided to come to this concert with an unlimited ammo gatling gun and explosive CDs, because no rock concert is complete without a little fireworks and good ol fashioned genocide I guess.

Pedictably, NoN shows up and kidnaps Aerosmith (as opposed to just killing them). You fight off waves of discount power ranger baddies to reach Aerosmiths dressing room where you are told that music is a weapon and then the image tosses you keys to Aerosmiths ride, a sweet black Ferarri (I'll give you a moment to put your eyes back in socket, I'm pretty sure they have rolled out by now). Remember kids, when shit gets censored, genocide is ALWAYS the answer.

So what kind of sub-human green lit this game for a Snes port? Well it was the head honchos a the now defunt Acclaim. So someone in upper management said "hey, do 40 year old rocker burnouts play Snes ? Aerosmith is still in with teens also, right?" Mind you this game was released in the mid 90s, when fanny packs were still popular and boy bands roamed the earth. (and Nickelodeon was god)

Just this alone should raise red flags; thier target audience was so small that you could have made a game about punching orphans and it would have had wider appeal. I guess this is why I saw this game at Funcoland years later with the price tag on 45 cents...about 45 cents more than it was worth.

So where do I start with this title?

I guess with the games most significant problem: The controls. So, someone decided that it was an amazing idea to NOT include lightgun compatibility for any of the console ports Instead opting to use the Gamepads. This isn't always a kiss of death, there were games that had reasonably decent shooting controls with a gamepad though they are few and far between.

This game, however, is not one of them. The game has 3 settings for cursor sensitivity ranging from 1 and 2 being super stiff to 3 being the cursors coated with WD40 or butter. Hitting anything in this game accurately Is a test of patience to say the least. Either you hit your target or you just slide the shots across and merely graze them. This wouldn't be so mucha prtoblem if they say had powerups that made your bullets hit a wider area, but they can't even be assed to do that. Instead you get to thow CD's at your enemies. Yes, CD's; a weapon less lethal than getting hit with a frisbe at the dog park.

Which brings me to he music. Do youself a favor and mute it immediately (alternatively cut your eats off with a CD...and no, it doesn't work; I tried.) Thankfully here (and in the video review at the bottom) I get to spare you the suffering. The games music loops in 15 second or so intervals and in some cases the game will put out terrible digitized lyrics that loop in 6 to 10 second intervals. I know the Snes has cart limitations, but if you can't fit it in, don't use it. Don't be lazy;make a few tracks that will fit instead of butchering already debatably bad Aerosmith songs. Listiening to this game is like being surrounded by police, except they keep blaring "Eat the Rich" and "Dude look like a lady" over the loud speakers. It's enough to make anyone cannibalize thier family as their mind slowly breaks(I suggets turning the console or sound off, I don't suggest eating your family; unless it's a Fallout kind of situatiom.)

And lastly we come to the graphics or in this case the lack of them. Most of the game has a washed over feel to it and it fails on many levels to utilize the Snes's color palette properly. Instead you get a whole lot of grey, brown black and yellow; Especially yellow since 90% of the enemies in game seem to have a death wish. Seriously, what kind of authoritarian regime dresses all the police in bright yellow? Did they go to the Naruto school of stealth? I can understand a show of power, but you can at least dress them in a color that doesn't scream "A stormtropper could hit me from 8 miles away" color. Worse yet the bosses don't even explode; they kind of just puff smoke and fly apart when they are defeated, as if vacating the game as quickly as possible.

I wish i could vacate with them, but I trudge along and suffer so you don't have to. I'm kinda like a Gandhi of retro gaming. No, not the peaceful one, the Civ 4 one aka an asshole.(Ok maybe not, If REALLY wanted the world to burn I would be giving this a positive review instead.)

In conclusion it's about as good as Aerosmiths last album, coughshitCough. Best left forgotten in a Gamestop Bargin bin somewhere and left far out of reach of those with depressive disorders (or if you really want, as a troll holidays gift for a sibling. Just prepare yourself for a possible beating later when they get around to playing it.)

Well, that was depressing. Everyday i tell myself "hey, retro games can't possibly get worse than X last game I played" only to be proven horribly wrong, further decresing my faith in humanity score (if it keeps getting negatives I will gain the "Lost the will to live" debuff)

I have been No Talent Redmage and this has been my review of Revolution X for the Snes. I would rather castrate myself witha rusty carving knife than ever play it ever again.

I'll see ya next time.
